 Election guide: What to know for the 2026 General Election in Wisconsin 
 By Juliana Tornabene Published : Oct. 23, 2026 at 9:16 AM CDT | Updated : 21 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google CHECK ELECTION RESULTS 
 MADISON, Wis. (WMTV) - The polls open at 7 a.m. Tuesday, Nov. 3 for the 2026 General Election in Wisconsin.
 WMTV 15 News has you covered with a voter guide on what to bring to the polls, where to find your polling place and how to turn in an absentee ballot.
 Where and when to vote
 The polls are open from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. on Election Day in Wisconsin. Voters just need to be in line at 8 p.m. to be able to vote.
 Voters can check the Wisconsin Elections Commission’s MyVote Wisconsin website to verify their registration, find their polling place and see what will be on their ballot.
 What to bring to the polls
 Voters must bring an acceptable photo ID to the polls, such as a driver’s license, state ID or U.S. passport. There is no separate voter ID in Wisconsin.
 The photo ID for voting does not need to show a voter’s current address.
 The Wisconsin Department of Transportation Division of Motor Vehicles said a REAL ID card is also not required for voting.
 If you need to register at the polls on Election Day, voters will need to bring a proof of address. The proof of address can be in electronic or paper format. Examples of accepted documents include a utility bill issued in the last 90 days, a bank statement and a current and valid driver’s license.
 Voting by mail? 
 Voters planning to vote by mail need to return their ballot as soon as possible before the deadline on Election Day, Nov. 3. 
 The deadline to request an absentee ballot is 5 p.m. Oct. 29 for regular or overseas voters. Those who are indefinitely confined or in the military and not away from home have until 5 p.m. Oct. 30 to make their request. 
 Voters who are hospitalized can request an appointed agent bring a ballot to them, if the patient is hospitalized seven days prior to the election. Those in the hospital can request an absentee ballot between Oct. 27 and Nov. 3 at 5 p.m. 
 Those in the military and who are away from home have until 5 p.m. Nov. 3 to request an absentee ballot. 
 What’s on your ballot
 Each ballot in Wisconsin will list the statewide race for Justice of the Supreme Court, as well as various county and local races. 
 You can check what races are on your ballot on MyVote Wisconsin .
